potential-positive-definite|couplingPote.annotation: The identity $h^TKh=h_0^2+h_1^2+(h_0+h_1)^2$ gives a direct reason for the formal positivity claim. If $h\ne0$, one of the first two squares is positive. Among unit vectors, the sum is smallest when $h_0=-h_1$ and the last square vanishes. In the undamped equal-mass model this is the slow oscillation direction: the masses move in the same physical direction and the middle spring keeps its length (Section 6).

test-inequality|le_of_littleO|1.annotation: For a point $a+h$ satisfying the remainder bound, $f(a+h)-f(a)\ge \tfrac12Q(h)-|R(h)|\ge0$. The factor $C/2$ comes from the Taylor coefficient $1/2!$. In Section 3, the surrounding proof chooses a neighbourhood where that bound on $R$ holds at every point.

lean-smoothness|coercive_of_posdef_of_co.annotation: This second call uses smoothness to identify the half polar form of $Q$ with $B(u,v)=D^2f(a)[u,v]$ for arbitrary $u,v$. The resulting lower bound concerns $B(h,h)$ alone, which the first call obtains directly by minimising on the unit sphere and scaling (Section 2).
